description: We are FlameFrags!, an enthusiastic team of developers, data nerds, and designers from Bahrain for the NASA Space Apps Challenge! Inspired by the Flame in Freefall initiative, we build user-friendly software to visualize, track, and manage vital scientific data that heads to Space and beyond. By blending coding, data, and graphic design, we turn complex space telemetry into clear insights while pushing our boundaries as a team. 🚀🔥
summary: FlameFrags is an interactive scientific platform focused on understanding combustion in microgravity and its implications for future human space exploration. Drawing on NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics research, it combines AI-assisted scientific exploration, experimental data analysis, combustion comparisons, research-gap detection, and interactive flame visualizations. Its habitat relevance tools connect combustion research to environments such as the ISS, lunar habitats, and Mars missions. Alongside the main dashboard, FlameFrags features a standalone Historical VR Explorer, allowing users to immerse themselves in 3D recreations of Apollo 1, Apollo 13, and Mir to explore three significant spacecraft fire-related events. By bringing together scientific data, analytical tools, AI, and immersive historical exploration, FlameFrags aims to make space-combustion research more accessible and help users investigate the challenges of fire safety beyond Earth.
details:
FlameFrags: Flame in Freefall Hub

1. Project Overview & Objective

Spacecraft, space stations, and future planetary habitats operate in extreme environments where fire safety is a critical life-support concern. However, decades of valuable microgravity combustion research—collected across NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) programs—remain locked inside complex, raw dataset archives that are difficult for students, educators, and non-specialists to parse.

Our mission is to transform complex NASA microgravity combustion data into an accessible, interactive, and intelligent scientific platform that bridges space research with real-world crew training and terrestrial safety.

2. Core Architecture & System Modules

FlameFrags combines four complementary components into a unified orbital intelligence hub:

  1. Grounded AI Research Assistant (Frags AI & Experiment Detective): Powered by the Gemini API, our assistant analyzes 24+ NASA PSI combustion investigations (including ACME, FLEX, BASS-II, SoFIE, and Saffire). Every insight features a visible Evidence Chain citing specific source experiments, fuel types, oxygen ranges, and dataset rows, alongside live statistical audits (outlier detection and correlations).
  2. Interactive NASA PSI Data Archive & Gap Detector: Users can inspect curated scientific data (.csv, .xlsx, .txt) or upload custom experimental logs. The platform automatically runs quality audits, generates a Combustion DNA scientific fingerprint for each experiment, and uses a Research Gap Detector to map underrepresented atmospheric and partial-gravity regimes.
  3. Real-Time 0G vs. 1G Physics & Habitat Bridge: A Three.js interactive visualizer contrasts Earth's buoyant teardrop flames against microgravity's spherical diffusion flames and cool flames. Users can merge experimental profiles into a FlameTwin comparison and scale combustion risks across ISS, Lunar Gateway, and Martian habitats.
  4. 3D ISS Microgravity Fire Drill Simulation: A full-screen, first-person 3D simulation of an 18-module International Space Station interior (including Destiny, Node 3, and the Cupola). Users float through zero-gravity inertial drift, respond to cabin smoke alarms, don Protective Breathing Equipment (PBE) masks, and execute emergency suppression protocols with fine-water-mist and CO2 extinguishers.

3. Tech Stack & Development Toolkit

Our platform is built using modern web and spatial technologies, including TypeScript, React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, and @react-three/fiber for custom GLSL shaders and zero-g physics. We integrate the Google Gemini API for scientific natural language reasoning and Supabase for database management. Development workflows incorporate automated Vitest unit testing for station hatch collision logic, paired with physical acoustic flame-extinguishment hardware benchmarking.

4. Innovation & Creative Approach

FlameFrags goes beyond traditional static data dashboards by blending empirical NASA science, interactive multi-variable flame simulation, and immersive 3D emergency training into a single ecosystem.

Instead of simple text queries, our Combustion DNA fingerprints and FlameTwin workbenches allow users to visualize and merge complex experimental variables dynamically. Furthermore, we maintain strict architectural transparency, explicitly separating verified empirical NASA measurements from simulated AI interpolations and multi-gravity habitat extrapolations.

5. Target Audience & Real-World Impact

FlameFrags targets aerospace students, educators, researchers, and space-exploration enthusiasts seeking to understand fluid dynamics and safety engineering in microgravity.

Beyond space exploration, our platform highlights critical terrestrial spillovers—demonstrating how ISS fine-water-mist suppression tech safeguards AI data centers and hospital ICUs, and how low-flow combustion models improve wildfire ember prediction and EV battery fire containment. Future development will expand automated dataset processing and hardware sensor integrations.

6. Engineering & Design Principles

During development, our team prioritized three core pillars:

  • Scientific Rigor & Transparency: Ensuring AI outputs never hallucinate data by tethering every response to verifiable NASA PSI source links and confidence tiers.
  • Performance & Accessibility: Optimizing Three.js rendering performance, smooth pointer-lock camera controls, and responsive UI layouts so users can seamlessly transition between deep data analysis and 3D simulation on desktop and mobile devices.
  • Multi-Environment Adaptability: Structuring all physics engines and fire safety SOPs to scale cleanly across microgravity, lunar, and martian acceleration parameters.

7. Virtual Reality

FragsVR lets the user look at spacecrafts like the Apollo 1, Apollo 13 and Mir space station, informing the user what caused the issue, why it happened and how to prevent it in the future. FragsVR uses -

  • WebXR & XRBlocks (src/index.ts, src/xr/): Powers full immersive VR device integration, managing controllers, hand tracking, local-floor reference spaces, and proper near/far clipping planes for accurate cockpit scaling.
  • Spatial VR Panel (src/three/SpatialVRPanel.ts): Renders an in-world floating HUD console directly inside VR environments to let you handle crew timeline steps, mission navigation, and inspection data in 3D.
  • Mobile Stereoscopic VR Mode: Uses a split-screen stereoscopic rendering pipeline with adjustable interpupillary distance (IPD) scaling built for mobile VR setups (such as using a Samsung Gear VR with sensor-streaming apps).
  • Multi-Mode Head Tracking (src/xr/WebcamHeadTracker.ts): Provides an optical tracking fallback using native FaceDetector (with a skin/head-weighted YCbCr centroid fallback) for hands-free head-look navigation.
